items.title: Replay Before You Reply: Second-Look Prompting for Unified Multimodal Encoding
items.abs: Solving multimodal tasks requires Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to form a unified understanding of the image and the question text. However, under causal attention in current VLMs, a token can attend only to what precedes it. Whichever modality comes first is therefore encoded under partial observation of the input, uninformed by the rest of the multimodal context. We introduce Second-Look Prompting (SLP), a training-free method that repeats the image-question pair in the input. In the repeated copy, every visual and textual token can attend to the complete input, yielding a unified multimodal encoding of the pair. Moreover, the added visual tokens contribute computation beyond re-exposing the image: even a blank image in their place can improve reasoning. Across 12 benchmarks, SLP improves the overall average score of every evaluated model, spanning nine open-source models (3B-72B) and three proprietary frontier models, with gains reaching 5.6 points for Gemini 3 Flash on MATH-Vision.

items.abs: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). However, most of them encode a sample of past frames again at every decision and are trained on isolated decisions, so computation is redundant and the usable history is short. They also learn from their own mistakes through outcome rewards that give one scalar to a whole episode. items.title: Towards an Armenian Epigraphic Corpus
items.abs: The Divan hay vimagrut'yan (1960-2017), the printed corpus of Armenian inscriptions, comprises nearly 7,600 records; a growing number of the inscriptions they describe, damaged or destroyed in recent decades, survive only in its pages. Armenian epigraphy nevertheless lacks a digital resource of the kind available for Greek, Latin or Georgian. This paper presents the Corpus Inscriptionum Armenicarum Electronicum, which turns the ten volumes of the Divan into an open digital corpus. Layout detection, OCR and a vision-language model produce a first structured reading of each record, which specialists then check on a proofreading platform. First corrections show that letters are read reliably and that residual errors concentrate in the editorial signs. The corpus is designed as a lasting platform for documenting Armenian inscriptions and as a source of silver data in Classical and Middle Armenian for language models and computational linguistics.

items.abs: Video corpus moment retrieval (VCMR) requires finding the video and time interval that match a text query in a corpus of videos. items.title: DexLatentWorld: 3D Cross-Embodiment Latent Action World Models for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation
items.abs: World models facilitate planning and control in robotic manipulation by enabling agents to anticipate the consequences of their actions. However, they typically rely on action-labelled interaction data that is costly to acquire and difficult to scale. These models are also often tied to the specific embodiment they were trained on, limiting transferability to previously unseen robot morphologies. We introduce a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations. items.abs: Deploying large vision-language-action (VLA) models on resource-constrained robots demands extreme compression, yet existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods frequently collapse at ultra-low bit-widths ($\le$ 2 bits). items.title: Inclusive Hand Pose Estimation via Topology-Aware Distillation and Progressive Kinematic Reasoning
items.abs: Hand pose estimation aims to recover the spatial configuration of hand joints from visual observations and serves as a fundamental perception module for downstream systems that rely on complete and topologically consistent hand representations. Most existing methods are developed under the assumption of fully articulated hand structures and tend to produce unstable or implausible predictions when parts of the kinematic structure are persistently absent, resulting in degraded performance or even system failure despite available partial observations. To study this challenge, we construct IncNYU, a physiologically constrained benchmark that simulates structural incompleteness through morphological modification of complete hand models and retains reference locations for both intact and synthetically removed regions. items.title: Action Windows Are Inherently Temporal: A Benchmark for Time-Sensitive Robotic Manipulation
items.abs: Vision-language model (VLM) agents have surpassed learned-policy baselines on existing robotic manipulation benchmarks. However, these agents still struggle with time-sensitive everyday tasks that existing benchmarks for VLM agents cover only partially. In these tasks, evolving physical processes create finite windows for successful intervention. These action windows are inherently temporal and impose a shared time budget on decision making and physical execution. Coordinating intervention within this budget requires agents to determine when the window opens. We introduce AWAIT, a simulation benchmark that evaluates task completion within action windows while accounting for decision and execution time. Our evaluation reveals difficulties in recognizing window onset and shows that successive decisions and movements can exhaust an action window even when each decision takes less than the window duration. items.abs: Vision-language models (VLMs) extract structured data from documents by generating the requested JSON one token at a time, so their sequential steps grow with the length of the answer. items.title: VistaTree: Question Answering over Long Multimodal Documents with Image-Derived Summary Trees
items.abs: Answering questions over long multimodal documents requires locating relevant evidence across pages containing text, tables, and figures. When the document exceeds the model's context window, selective retrieval becomes necessary. We introduce VistaTree, a document question-answering agent that builds a summary tree directly from rendered page images. VistaTree segments documents into contiguous page spans, recursively groups them into a topic hierarchy, and refines sibling summaries to distinguish neighboring sections. At query time, the agent uses node summaries to select relevant nodes and reads the corresponding pages, using hierarchical navigation when the full outline exceeds the context budget. Experiments on MMLongBench-Doc and LongDocURL evaluate answer quality and retrieval cost using a locally hosted vision-language model, and quantify the performance gap between global and hierarchical access to the index.

items.abs: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). items.title: InterBand-EMG: A Cross-Band Foundation Model for Generalizable Hand-Pose Estimation
items.abs: Surface electromyography (sEMG) enables continuous hand-pose estimation, but learning representations that generalize across users and movements remains challenging. We introduce InterBand-EMG, which combines band-specific quantization with cross-band reconstruction and structured masked code prediction to learn transferable EMG representations for hand-pose tracking. We also introduce SynapMyo, an eight-channel EMG-to-pose dataset comprising 1,227.74 hand-hours from 499 users across 68 movement categories. Experiments on emg2pose and SynapMyo show that InterBand-EMG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in joint-angle accuracy across all three generalization settings on both datasets. The source code and the SynapMyo dataset will be publicly released upon acceptance of this paper.

items.title: EgoSurgHands: An Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Dataset & Benchmark for Open Surgery Training
items.abs: Surgical skill assessment, AR guidance, and robot learning from demonstration all benefit from 3D tracking of the surgeon's hands, yet no surgical dataset offers real egocentric articulated 3D hand pose. We introduce EgoSurgHands, a benchmark for real-captured egocentric hand pose estimation in open surgery training on synthetic pads. Captured with multi-sensor glasses, it contains 41,909 training hand-instance rows across 55 procedure recordings and 9,476 human-validated evaluation rows across 13 held-out recordings, spanning 13 tasks, 3 glove colors, and 4 trainees from first-year medical student to third-year resident. Each frame carries a multi-sensor stack: intrinsics, hand landmarks with per-hand confidence, timestamps, and eye gaze, plus SLAM extrinsics where SLAM succeeded. items.title: Defending Vision-Language-Action Models against Transferable Attacks via Visual-Proprioceptive Consistency
items.abs: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong capabilities in a wide range of robotic tasks. Motivated by this observation, we propose a proprioception-grounded defense framework that leverages trusted proprioceptive information to detect and mitigate transferable adversarial attacks. Specifically, we utilize the robot's proprioceptive states to establish a trusted spatial reference, and compare it with the robot's perceived location inferred from visual features. items.abs: As humanoid robots increasingly enter real-world environments, recovering their 3D whole-body pose from monocular imagery is becoming increasingly important for external state perception, motion analysis, and robot learning. items.title: RoboColiseum: Co-evolution of Simulation, Evaluation, and Models
items.abs: Simulation-based evaluation of embodied models requires calibrated interactions, diverse tasks, and explicit execution constraints. We present RoboColiseum, a platform combining system identification, composable physics and rendering, and multidimensional benchmarking. Recorded-command replay characterizes robot dynamics and object interactions, while a shared interface connects rigid and deformable simulation to rendering. Across 22 paired real--simulation robot--task configurations, task scores have a reported Pearson correlation of 0.9686. Eight evaluation tracks span instruction following, spatial reasoning, general manipulation, robustness, dexterous manipulation, precision manipulation, whole-body coordination, and execution across robot embodiments. Budget-aware scoring combines task progress, resource use, and completion rewards. items.abs: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews. At ICLR, measured overlap rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, in reviews from the same stage of the review process, with year-on-year rises at NeurIPS, ICML and the F1000 and PLOS journals. items.abs: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. items.title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
items.abs: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. items.abs: Agent skills are documents in which experts write down procedural knowledge, and models increasingly maintain them by rewriting them without feedback. items.abs: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. items.abs: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. items.abs: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. items.abs: Recent advances in robotic manipulation have enabled increasingly complex and dexterous behaviors, yet existing benchmarks still focus on simple pick-and-place tasks and lack a systematic framework for measuring progress in robot learning along the axis of task difficulty. items.abs: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. items.abs: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. items.abs: Mamba-based methods for video-based 3D human pose estimation can model long sequences with linear complexity, but their selective state updates usually lack direct exploitation of skeletal relations. Meanwhile, stacking modeling blocks at the full temporal resolution leads to high computational overhead, while compressing the temporal sequence makes it difficult to retain per-frame details. items.title: CJRR-Net: A Candidate-Joint Reprojection Ranking for Future-View Selection in Human Pose Estimation
items.abs: Multi-camera systems support performance recording, sports and human-movement analysis, where selecting an informative viewpoint is important for reliable human pose estimation. We propose the Candidate-Joint Reprojection Ranking Network (CJRR-Net) for future-view selection among eight calibrated cameras in MPI-INF-3DHP. The model combines current-view pose observations, camera configuration, and candidate-specific geometric features obtained by reprojecting the estimated 3D pose and its uncertainty into each candidate view. CJRR-Net achieves a selected-view 2D mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) of 105.18 pixels, compared with 114.64 pixels for the shared-input MLP and 117.56 pixels for adapted PoseErrNet. It also achieves the lowest mean error among the listed policies in each evaluated occlusion group. A blender rollout illustrates repeated camera selection. These findings support candidate-specific geometry for single-view selection in the evaluated fixed eight-camera setting.

items.abs: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. items.abs: Egocentric auto-labeling requires depth, camera pose, object, and human-pose estimates to agree across independently developed models. items.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
items.abs: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. items.abs: Modern visuotactile sensors primarily sense contact by imaging the deformation of a compliant interface. Using techniques such as photometric stereo, they can recover detailed contact geometry, often represented as surface normals or depth. However, force-related information typically still needs to be inferred indirectly through calibration, geometric reconstruction, or learned mappings. Mechanochromic photonic-crystal (PC) materials offer an alternative physical encoding mechanism: contact loading changes their periodic microstructure and spectral response, directly transforming local stress into a spatially resolved structural-color field. Despite this potential, PC materials have rarely been explored as visuotactile sensors for closed-loop robot learning. items.title: Embodied First Exam
items.abs: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. items.abs: Dexterous hands enable versatile manipulation, but policies trained in simulation often degrade on hardware owing to non-idealities, and the high-dimensional action space makes real-world adaptation costly. We propose GAP (Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing), a sample-efficient adaptation framework that learns how to adapt, rather than how to act, during simulation pretraining and transfers this adaptation prior to hardware. Between repeated executions, GAP uses feedback to adjust the actions of the next one: a gradient guidance network learns from paired executions how adjusting actions affects playing performance, and its gradients guide these adjustments. items.abs: Dexterous grasping in robotics relies on distinct hand configurations depending on object geometry. We introduce BetaGrasp, a 3D diffusion policy that conditions a DP3-style point-cloud policy on a four-class grasp label (crimp, sloper, pinch, and jug), running on a Franka arm with a 16-DoF LEAP hand. We also introduce a climbing-hold benchmark: a spring testbed whose ratchet gives a slip-force reading in newtons. In our analysis the policy's point-cloud encoder did not separate the four holds, so the scan alone gave it little to choose a grasp from. Without the label (a DP3-style baseline), simulated rollouts from the robot's reset pose all end in a jug grasp, whatever the hold (25% correct grasp type, versus 94% for BetaGrasp). The label works as a switch for which grasp the policy performs. On 80 paired hardware trials, BetaGrasp raises average slip force from 9.6 N to 14.3 N, and grasps slipping fully off the hold drop from 44% of trials to 10%.

items.abs: Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. items.abs: Dexterous manipulation with world action models (WAMs) relies on hand configuration and contact information, yet joint-state and whole-hand tactile observations may be partially or entirely missing. items.abs: Generative robot policies based on diffusion and flow matching can model complex, multimodal behaviors, but remain susceptible to covariate shift during closed-loop execution. We introduce GUARD, an anomaly-informed Q-steering framework that leverages the policy's training distribution to construct a dense, failure-anticipatory steering signal. GUARD pairs sparse task rewards with dense anomaly scores learned from policy training data and propagates both through a learned Q-function. items.abs: We present RevoSim, a scalable and high-fidelity multimodal tactile simulator for the BrainCo Revo3 hand that jointly models 285 piezoresistive taxels and five visuotactile fingertips. This dissertation presents an open-source 3D-printed arm which was assembled and programmed on two fronts. items.abs: World-action models (WAMs) such as Cosmos 3 jointly generate future video and robot actions from an observation and instruction. items.title: Neuromotor Hierarchy Network: Physiological Inductive Biases for Robust Generalization in sEMG Decoding
items.abs: Surface electromyography (sEMG) provides a wearable, noninvasive interface to neuromuscular activity for movement decoding and human-computer interaction. Population-scale decoding remains difficult because the relationship between sEMG and neuromuscular activity varies across users and sessions, while task-relevant dynamics span channels and multiple timescales. Learning waveform-to-output mappings from task labels leaves the distinction between recording variability and coordinated motor activity implicit. We introduce the Neuromotor Hierarchy Network (NHN), which learns a compact latent neuromotor state from task supervision to represent task-relevant neuromuscular coordination. items.title: EMG-GPT: Predictive Pretraining on Residual-Quantized EMG Tokens for Hand Pose Estimation
items.abs: Surface electromyography (sEMG) is a low-power, cost-effective biosignal for hand-pose estimation and gesture classification. In this work, we examine whether self-supervised pretraining on sEMG can yield transferable representations for continuous hand-pose estimation. We introduce EMG-GPT, a causal transformer-based model that operates on discrete sEMG representations from a frozen residual vector quantization (RVQ) tokenizer and learns temporal dynamics through depth-autoregressive future-code prediction. The model combines within-frame integration with causal temporal modeling while preserving the geometry of the pretrained codebook. EMG-GPT shows competitive results in both Regression and Tracking tasks, supporting EMG-only pretraining as a viable approach for learning transferable sEMG representations.

items.title: Now You Feel It, Now You See Me: Digital-Twin-based Teleoperation Interface for Dexterous Manipulation
items.abs: Teleoperation is becoming increasingly important for collecting high-quality demonstrations to teach robots dexterous manipulation skills. For dexterous manipulation, bare-hand tracking provides a practical way to control robotic hands and demonstrate coordinated finger movements without gloves or exoskeletons. However, this type of teleoperation faces two key feedback limitations: a lack of force feedback and visual feedback of occluded region. The absence of force feedback hinders precise and safe manipulation, as operators must infer contact force visually rather than feel them directly. Occlusion by objects or other robot parts impairs the assessment of hand positions, approach distances, and pre-grasp configurations suited to the object's shape. items.abs: Egocentric bimanual hand pose estimation is important for virtual interaction, wearable control, and rehabilitation, but visual observations are often degraded by self-occlusion, hand-hand contact, and object manipulation. items.abs: Multimodal 3D Human Pose Estimation (3D HPE) combines complementary information from RGB, LiDAR, and mmWave radar, but models trained on correlated observations from the same individuals, raise privacy risks overlooked by record level analysis. items.abs: Vision foundation models such as DINOv2, SigLIP2, and MASt3R develop complementary capabilities from different pretraining objectives, yet their knowledge remains distributed across separate, specialized models. Multi-teacher knowledge distillation offers a path toward consolidating these capabilities into a single agglomerative backbone, but existing approaches assume a fixed set of teachers, and incorporating a new teacher requires repeating expensive joint distillation over the entire teacher set. We introduce GRAFT, a continual multi-teacher distillation framework that enables a unified backbone to progressively acquire capabilities from an open-ended sequence of foundation models. items.abs: World-space hand motion estimation from egocentric video requires recovering 3D articulated hand geometry while tracking camera egomotion. items.abs: Reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can train dexterous manipulation policies without robot demonstrations, but training a single generalist policy with task-agnostic rewards faces a severe exploration problem: approaching, grasping, and reorienting diverse objects with many degrees of freedom is difficult to discover from scratch. Prior works make exploration tractable with high-quality robot demonstrations, per-task reward shaping, or by restricting policies to narrow modes of behavior. items.title: ESTHER: Egocentric Stereo Hand Estimation and Reconstruction in the Wild
items.abs: Human dexterity is guided by two eyes watching two hands: binocular vision supplies the metric 3D structure that fine-grained manipulation consumes. Egocentric stereo is therefore the natural perceptual interface for robots, AR, and VR-yet metric 3D hand reconstruction from this very signal still has neither an end-to-end model nor an in-the-wild benchmark. items.abs: Current methods for egocentric view action recognition often face challenges in perceiving dynamic hand movements relying solely on geometrical or physical information. items.abs: Automated quality assessment of rehabilitation exercises relies heavily on accurate human pose estimation from video data. Although numerous RGB-based pose estimation methods have been proposed, the impact of camera placement on detecting clinically relevant movement errors remains insufficiently explored. items.abs: Human demonstrations are a cheap source of data for dexterous manipulation, but co-training a robot policy on them requires closing the human--robot gap in every modality the policy consumes. items.abs: Monocular RGB-based hand pose estimation has emerged as a critical research frontier in computer vision. items.abs: Monocular 3D human pose estimation (HPE) remains challenging due to depth ambiguity, occlu- sions, and the need for temporal consistency. While multi-view methods provide superior accuracy over monocular approaches, they often require complex setups. The approach leverages DSTformer, a monocular feature extractor, to capture long-range pose dependencies within each view. A fusion transformer then aggregates information across views to produce coherent 3D estimates. items.abs: Foundation models are endowing autonomous systems with greater intelligence, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of the environment through visual perception. A representative example is Human Mesh Recovery (HMR), which provides useful estimates of a target's 3D pose and shape that can benefit tactical missions. However, the size and power demands of such models make them difficult to run on edge platforms and limit their real-time performance, undermining the requirements of tactical edge deployment - especially for active perception, where a mobile robot must plan its next-best view on-board and cannot offload computation under contested communications. items.abs: Pretraining Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies on internet-scale video is appealing, yet current latent-action objectives often learn the wrong thing: they remain anchored to pixel variation rather than action-relevant state transitions, making them vulnerable to appearance bias, nuisance motion, and information leakage. We introduce VLA-JEPA, a JEPA-style pretraining framework that sidesteps these pitfalls by design. items.abs: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) may memorize private, copyrighted, or unsafe visual information, making selective unlearning essential for their responsible deployment. items.title: Spatial Bias in Vision Language Models
items.abs: Spatial intelligence is essential for embodied tasks such as navigation, manipulation, and agentic interaction. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly exhibit spatial reasoning capabilities, yet priors learned from large-scale vision-language pre-training may override current visual evidence and induce systematic spatial errors. While social bias and visual hallucination have been widely studied, spatial bias remains underexplored. We define spatial bias as the systematic tendency of VLMs toward prior-aligned spatial predictions despite conflicting visual evidence. To investigate this phenomenon, we construct an original--counterfactual embodied visual question answering (VQA) benchmark covering diverse spatial tasks and prior sources, and introduce a multi-stage diagnostic framework that distinguishes counterfactual failures from prior-retention bias, language-aligned bias, and non-bias errors. items.title: Scaling Wrist sEMG for Hand Pose Estimation
items.abs: Surface electromyography (sEMG) offers a promising alternative to vision for hand pose estimation, providing information that is complementary to visual observations. However, unlike vision, sEMG-based hand pose estimation has received limited attention. In this work, we present CycloFormer, a rotation-invariant Transformer that encodes the cyclic symmetry of the wrist-worn sEMG electrode ring into its architecture. It achieves state-of-the-art landmark-distance performance on emg2pose, and exhibits systematic scaling with model size and training data. Through comparison with the leading vision baseline, we show that an sEMG-based pose-estimation pipeline becomes more accurate when visual evidence is limited. We also derive a scaling law for sEMG hand-pose regression in the data-scarce regime. It identifies the loss-minimising model size at the current data scale and suggests that large-scale data collection is a key direction for advancing sEMG-based hand pose estimation.

items.title: COCOA: Action-Conditioned Correction for Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.abs: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance on complex robot manipulation tasks by generating low-level action chunks from multimodal observations and language instructions. However, an erroneous action chunk can derail long-horizon execution and lead to task failure. items.abs: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are typically trained with embodiment-specific motor commands, creating a mismatch between rich multimodal representations and the low-level signals used for action supervision. items.abs: Despite advances in policy pretraining, embodied AI systems can plateau during task-specific fine-tuning as uniform scenario collection encounters fewer of the remaining failures. items.abs: Diffusion and flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies achieve strong robotic control through repeated model evaluations to progressively refine actions, but such multi-step inference introduce substantial latency. items.abs: Recovering 3D human body motion from video is important for applications such as rehabilitation assessment and sports performance evaluation. items.abs: In this paper, we propose \textbf{Gestalt}, a new paradigm of large multimodal model built around multimodal interplay. items.abs: 3D hand mesh reconstruction is a challenging yet essential task for downstream applications, including human-robot interaction and AR/VR.
